variants.title: Calculate the error rate
variants.context: An error rate is failed requests divided by total requests, expressed as a percentage.
variants.prompt: Of 1000 requests, 20 fail. What percentage failed?
variants.hint: Divide failures by all requests, then multiply by 100.

variants.title: Look beyond the median
variants.context: In this exercise, exactly 99% of requests meet the latency threshold. The remaining 1% exceed it.
variants.prompt: Exactly 99% of 10000 requests finish within 300 ms. How many take longer?
variants.explanation: 1% of 10000 is 100. A healthy median can hide these slow requests.

variants.title: Measure the user outcome
variants.context: A useful metric distinguishes a fast success from a fast failure and exposes waiting.
variants.prompt: Average latency falls from 200 ms to 50 ms because requests now fail immediately. What must accompany latency?
options: Only the latency of failed requests.
Only the average request body size.
variants.hint: Measure the part of the journey where the symptom occurs.
variants.explanation: Fast failures reduce latency without serving users. Track successful outcomes too.
